+        text_chunks = re.findall(self.compiled_pattern, text)

+        if vocab_size <= 0x110000:
+            # every token id fits in one code point: train on one str holding
+            # all chunks (bytes as code points) joined by "\xff", a byte that

+            b = b"\xff".join([ch.encode("utf-8") for ch in text_chunks])

+            merges = {}
+            vocab = {idx: bytes([idx]) for idx in range(256)}
+            _train_sep_str(b.decode("latin-1"), num_merges, stats, heap,
+                           merges, vocab, verbose)

+            self.vocab = vocab

+def _train_sep_str(s, num_merges, stats, heap, merges, vocab, verbose):
+    # like BasicTokenizer._train_str, but pairs touching the "\xff" chunk
+    # separator (code point 255, never a token of a chunk) are not counted
+    stats_get = stats.get
+    for i in range(num_merges):
+        top, cands = pop_top_pairs(heap, stats_get, heappush, heappop)
+        if len(cands) == 1:
+            pair = cands[0]
+        else:
+            best = -1
+            for p in cands:
+                j = s.find(chr(p[0]) + chr(p[1]))
+                if best < 0 or j < best:
+                    best = j
+                    pair = p
+        idx = 256 + i
+        p0, p1 = pair
+        ps = chr(p0) + chr(p1)
+        find = s.find
+        pos = []
+        pos_app = pos.append
+        j = find(ps)
+        while j >= 0:
+            pos_app(j)
+            j = find(ps, j + 2)
+        n = len(s)
+        k = len(pos)
+        removed = [pair]
+        rapp = removed.append
+        added = set()
+        aadd = added.add
+        prev_end = -1
+        for m in range(k):
+            j = pos[m]
+            if j and j != prev_end:
+                a = ord(s[j-1])
+                if a != 255:
+                    p = (a, p0)
+                    stats[p] -= 1
+                    rapp(p)
+                    p = (a, idx)
+                    stats[p] = stats_get(p, 0) + 1
+                    aadd(p)
+            if j + 2 < n:
+                b = ord(s[j+2])
+                if b != 255:
+                    p = (p1, b)
+                    stats[p] -= 1
+                    rapp(p)
+                    if m + 1 < k and pos[m+1] == j + 2:
+                        b = idx
+                    p = (idx, b)
+                    stats[p] = stats_get(p, 0) + 1
+                    aadd(p)
+            prev_end = j + 2
+        stats[pair] -= k
+        for p in removed:
+            if stats_get(p) == 0:
+                del stats[p]
+        for p in added:
+            heappush(heap, (-stats[p], p))
+        s = s.replace(ps, chr(idx))
+        merges[pair] = idx
+        vocab[idx] = vocab[p0] + vocab[p1]
+        if verbose:
+            print(f"merge {i+1}/{num_merges}: {pair} -> {idx} ({vocab[idx]}) had {top} occurrences")
+

@@ -0,0 +1,153 @@
+"""
+Encoding helpers (apply learned merges to a sequence of ids). Kept in their
+own module so that importing minbpe for training does not have to load them.
+"""
+from itertools import repeat
+
+
+def apply_merges(ids, merges, inf=None):
+    """
+    Repeatedly merge the pair with the lowest merge index until none applies.
+    Same result as min() over get_stats(ids) keyed by merges.get(p, inf): the
+    rank list is in position order, so .index() finds the first-seen pair
+    among the minimal ones, and the minimal rank is the merged token itself.
+    The rank list is computed once and then patched locally around each merged
+    occurrence (only the pairs touching a merged token change).
+    inf: optional "no merge" rank, must be greater than every value in merges;
+    defaults to float("inf").
+    """
+    if len(ids) < 2:
+        return ids
+    if len(ids) >= 256:
+        # long sequences: avoid the O(len) min/index/count scans per merge round
+        return _apply_merges_heap(ids, merges)
+    merges_get = merges.get
+    if inf is None:
+        inf = float("inf")
+    ranks = list(map(merges_get, zip(ids, ids[1:]), repeat(inf)))
+    ids = list(ids) # private copy: the single-occurrence path edits it in place
+    while ranks:
+        idx = min(ranks)
+        if idx == inf:
+            break # nothing else can be merged anymore
+        j = ranks.index(idx)
+        # positions with rank idx left to visit (all pair occurrences are among them)
+        k = ranks.count(idx)
+        if k == 1:
+            # single occurrence: splice it in place, recompute the neighbour ranks
+            ids[j] = idx
+            del ids[j+1]
+            del ranks[j]
+            if j:
+                ranks[j-1] = merges_get((ids[j-1], idx), inf)
+            if j < len(ranks):
+                ranks[j] = merges_get((idx, ids[j+1]), inf)
+            continue
+        p0 = ids[j]
+        p1 = ids[j+1]
+        last = len(ranks) - 1 # last pair position
+        newids = []
+        ext = newids.extend
+        app = newids.append
+        newranks = []
+        rext = newranks.extend
+        rapp = newranks.append
+        index = ranks.index
+        s = 0 # start of the not yet copied part of ids / ranks
+        first = True
+        while True:
+            k -= 1
+            if ids[j] == p0 and ids[j+1] == p1:
+                # merge the occurrence at j (same left-to-right order as merge())
+                if s < j:
+                    if not first:
+                        rapp(merges_get((idx, ids[s]), inf))
+                    rext(ranks[s:j-1])
+                    rapp(merges_get((ids[j-1], idx), inf))
+                    ext(ids[s:j])
+                elif not first:
+                    rapp(merges_get((idx, idx), inf))
+                app(idx)
+                first = False
+                s = j + 2
+                if j < last and ranks[j+1] == idx:
+                    k -= 1 # overlapping position j+1 is skipped
+                start = s
+            else:
+                start = j + 1
+            if not k:
+                break
+            j = index(idx, start)
+        if s <= last + 1:
+            rapp(merges_get((idx, ids[s]), inf))
+            rext(ranks[s:])
+            ext(ids[s:])
+        ids = newids
+        ranks = newranks
+    return ids
+
+
+def _apply_merges_heap(ids, merges):
+    """
+    Same result as apply_merges, for long sequences: a doubly linked list over
+    the original positions plus a heap of (rank, position) entries for every
+    mergeable adjacent pair, validated lazily when popped. Each round pops all
+    entries of the minimal rank in position order; the first valid one picks
+    the pair, whose occurrences are merged left to right like merge().
+    """
+    from heapq import heapify, heappop, heappush
+    merges_get = merges.get
+    n = len(ids)
+    val = list(ids)
+    nxt = list(range(1, n + 1)) # n means "no next"
+    prv = list(range(-1, n - 1)) # -1 means "no previous"
+    heap = [(r, i) for i, r in enumerate(map(merges_get, zip(val, val[1:])))
+            if r is not None]
+    heapify(heap)
+    while heap:
+        r = heap[0][0]
+        pair = None
+        last = -1
+        merged = []
+        rest = []
+        while heap and heap[0][0] == r:
+            p = heappop(heap)[1]
+            if p == last:
+                continue # duplicate entry (pops come out in position order)
+            last = p
+            v = val[p]
+            if v is None:
+                continue # position was merged away
+            q = nxt[p]
+            if q == n:
+                continue
+            pr = (v, val[q])
+            if merges_get(pr) != r:
+                continue # stale entry
+            if pair is None:
+                pair = pr
+            elif pr != pair:
+                rest.append(p) # another pair with the same rank: later round
+                continue
+            val[p] = r
+            val[q] = None
+            q2 = nxt[q]
+            nxt[p] = q2
+            if q2 < n:
+                prv[q2] = p
+            merged.append(p)
+        for p in rest:
+            heappush(heap, (r, p))
+        for p in merged:
+            a = prv[p]
+            if a >= 0:
+                rk = merges_get((val[a], r))
+                if rk is not None:
+                    heappush(heap, (rk, a))
+            b = nxt[p]
+            if b < n:
+                rk = merges_get((r, val[b]))
+                if rk is not None:
+                    heappush(heap, (rk, p))
+    return [v for v in val if v is not None]
+

journal.text:
I tried to cut train_ir on minbpe by reworking how merges are applied. I first edited regex.py in place. Then I moved the merge logic into a new minbpe/_apply.py, rewired base.py, basic.py and regex.py to use it, and replaced the old code in base.py.

The first evaluation built and gave identical outputs, but it was rejected for no improvement. train_ir went from 363266659 to 396372549, a ratio of 1.0911 against a required 0.9900. encode_ir also rose, with a ratio of 1.0108. The second evaluation I recorded, evaluation 3, failed to build. The test_encode_decode_identity tests failed for BasicTokenizer, RegexTokenizer and GPT4Tokenizer. I stopped without submitting anything.

I now think my heap-style merge path costs more than the original loop at these input sizes. I also think the _apply.py refactor broke encode/decode round-tripping.

Next time I should get the identity tests passing with the smallest possible diff before measuring. I should also profile the train loop to find where the instructions actually go, rather than assuming merge application dominates.
